To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) cannabis and cannabinoids acutely impair verbal learning and memory, attention, executive functions, and psychomotor function, (2) these impairments may persist in chronic users and in abstinent users, and (3) younger age of onset and higher frequency of use are associated with poorer performance.
cannabis use is consistently associated with impairments in verbal memory and attention, with some evidence of persisting deficits in these domains after abstinence.

acute intoxication with cannabis is associated with impairment in psychomotor function, verbal memory, attention and executive function, and that chronic use of cannabis is associated with impaired verbal memory and attention.
